info.title: NSE MT5 Bridge API
info.description:
**NSE Platform secure local bridge** — one endpoint per command. The bridge attaches to the client's local MetaTrader 5 terminal through the official native C++ IPC driver and exposes exactly the 90 NSE bridge commands documented below. All endpoints are uniform `POST` JSON calls returning `{ok, data}` envelopes; broker rejections carry the official MT5 retcode.

*Security:* bind is localhost-only by default; an optional `X-API-Key` gate is configurable; the platform talks to this bridge over an outbound-authenticated WebSocket channel (no inbound ports).

*Real-time:* `/ws/ui` streams ticks + account updates to the local dashboard.

post.description: Overall bridge status: version, uptime, MT5 state, server channel, command count.
Real MT5 connection state with a live terminal liveness probe (never derived from config).
Attach to the local MT5 terminal via the official C++ IPC driver. Resilient: bounded retries with backoff, stale-attach release, account-mismatch fail-safe.
Release the MT5 IPC handle (always attempts shutdown — safe when already disconnected).
Full disconnect + resilient reconnect cycle.
Terminal process information: name, company, paths, connected, trade permissions, maxbars.
MT5 driver version, terminal build and build date.
Broker server identity: server name, company, currency, configured UTC offset, tick latency probe.
Bridge identity for MCP/platform integration: protocol, transports, tool count, docs URLs.
Complete account snapshot: login, balance, equity, margins, leverage, currency, trade mode.
Current account balance in the account currency.
Live equity (balance + floating PnL).
Margin currently locked by open positions.
Margin available for new trades.
Margin level in percent (equity/margin*100). None when no positions are open.
Current floating profit/loss of all open positions.
Base currency of the account.
Account + terminal trading permissions (EA trading enabled, trade mode, margin call levels).
List broker symbols with optional filter, visibility and tradeability flags.
Full broker specification of one symbol (digits, point, tick size/value, volumes, stops levels...).
Live bid/ask (and last deal price) for a symbol.
Minimum price increment (trade_tick_size; falls back to point).
One point value for the symbol (e.g. 0.01 on XAUUSD 2-digit).
Number of price decimal digits.
Broker-reported spread (points) + live ask-bid spread (price).
Session statistics for the current trading session. Note: the official MT5 API does not expose hourly quote/trade session schedules — these are the live session aggregates the terminal exposes.
Trade constraints: volume min/max/step, stops/freeze levels, trade mode, filling, swaps, margins.
Latest bid/ask tick for a symbol with freshness + staleness assessment.
Current best bid price.
Current best ask price.
Last executed price from the tick; falls back to the latest M1 bar close when the broker does not stream last-trade prices (typical for FX).
Order book (DOM) snapshot via market_book. Empty when the broker provides no depth for the symbol.
Bid/ask spread series over the last N minutes from tick history + summary stats.
Tick volume of the latest tick and the newest M1 bar.
Symbols currently visible in the terminal's Market Watch panel.
Register a live tick subscription for a symbol. Ticks are pushed to both WebSocket channels (dashboard + NSE server) at the requested interval.
Broker candle history (copy_rates). Position mode by count, or range mode via from_utc. The still-forming current bar is included and marked; invalid OHLC rows are dropped and reported.
Tick history via copy_ticks_from (count mode) or copy_ticks_range (from/to mode).
The bridge's configured chart timeframe (MT5 API cannot read the GUI chart's timeframe).
All MT5 timeframes with their enum values (21 supported: M1..MN1).
Column-oriented OHLCV arrays for charting (time, open, high, low, close, tick_volume).
Indicator availability. The MT5 terminal API does not expose GUI chart indicators — the bridge reports its own supported indicator set for server-side computation.
Chart objects availability. The MT5 terminal API does not expose chart objects/drawings.
The bridge's active chart context: configured symbol/timeframe, selection state, tick freshness.
Candle history for several timeframes in one call (server-side MTF analysis support).
All open positions (optionally filtered by symbol; 'bot' filter keeps our magic only).
Full details of one open position by ticket.
Current floating profit/loss of one position.
Open volume (lots) of one position.
Current stop-loss and take-profit of one position.
Risk exposure: loss-at-SL (broker-native order_calc_profit) + stop distance in points.
Change stop-loss and/or take-profit of an open position (TRADE_ACTION_SLTP, retries, guarded).
Close one position by ticket (full or partial via volume). Ambiguous retcodes are re-checked against broker state — no duplicate closes.
Close every open position (optionally one symbol). Reports per-ticket failures.
All active pending orders (LIMIT/STOP), optionally filtered by symbol.
Order details by ticket — active book first, then trade history (filled/cancelled).
Lifecycle status of an order: active (PLACED) or terminal state from history.
Historical orders in a UTC window (default last 24h), optional symbol group filter.
Closed positions reconstructed from deal history (grouped by position_id): volume in/out, net profit, commission, swap, open/close times.
Executed deals in a UTC window with profit, commission, swap, entry type and reason.
Remove an active pending order (TRADE_ACTION_REMOVE).
Modify price/SL/TP/volume/expiration of an active pending order (TRADE_ACTION_MODIFY).
Execution forensics for a historical order: fill price vs requested price (slippage), fill time, deals, commission.
Market buy/sell with SL/TP, deviation and magic. Ambiguous fills are reconciled against broker truth before any failure is reported.
Market buy (long entry) with SL/TP.
Market sell (short entry) with SL/TP.
Place LIMIT/STOP order with pre-dispatch structural validation (volume bounds, entry side, stops/freeze distances, SL/TP geometry) — structurally-invalid requests are rejected BEFORE dispatch.
Close part of a position (volume < position volume).
Close a position and immediately open the opposite side with the same volume.
Set (or replace) the stop-loss of an open position, preserving its current TP.
Set (or replace) the take-profit of an open position, preserving its current SL.
Broker-native PnL calculation for a hypothetical exit (order_calc_profit).
Optimal lot size for a risk budget (% of balance or fixed amount) and a stop distance. Rounded DOWN to the broker volume step.
Money at risk for a volume and stop (broker-native order_calc_profit with formula fallback).
SL price for a side and stop distance in points, tick-size aligned.
TP price for a side and reward distance in points, tick-size aligned.
Broker-native margin for a volume/price (order_calc_margin).
Predicted margin level (equity / projected margin * 100) if the trade is opened.
Account-currency value of one pip for a volume (pip = 10*point). Uses broker-native order_calc_profit as the source of truth, tick-value formula as fallback.
Broker-native PnL for a hypothetical entry/exit (order_calc_profit).
Full pre-trade validation WITHOUT dispatching: structural geometry (volume/SL/TP/stops distances vs live tick) + broker-side order_check + permission state.
Last recorded MT5 error (code + message) and the live driver last_error.
Recent bridge log entries (ring buffer) with optional level filter. Full files live in logs/bridge.log (rotated) and logs/bridge.jsonl (structured).
Health check summary: MT5 liveness, error rates, server channel, subscriptions.
Per-operation latency statistics (avg/max/last) for every MT5 call the bridge performs.
Connection state + full per-op MT5 call metrics + recent call ring (50 ops).
Order dispatch telemetry: sent/done/rejected/unknown, latencies, retcode histogram, recent orders.
Full capability manifest: every registered command, versions, supported features.
Every command as an MCP tool descriptor with its JSON-schema input (server-side MCP tool registration source).
Comprehensive one-shot troubleshooting dump: bridge, connection, terminal, account, metrics, recent calls, recent logs, subscriptions.
